---
title: "Certificate format"
subtitle: "What a front certificate proves, its syntax, and versions 1 and 2"
---

A certificate lists one plan per front point and one lower bound per gap between consecutive
points. A checker that verifies its four obligations has proved that the list is the Pareto front,
without trusting the solver ([Theorem 9.1](../proofs.qmd#node-theorem-9-1)). `zeno --certificate
FILE` writes one, `zeno check FILE` verifies it ([command line](cli.qmd#check)), and so does the
Lean checker `zeno-check`, whose acceptance is backed by a kernel-checked soundness theorem
([Lean tools](lean.qmd#zeno-check)).

The rest of this page is `doc/certificate-format.md`, the specification both checkers follow,
included as it stands in the repository.

## A small certificate

`zeno -n 2 -t 5 -p 2 -d tests/golden/data/lpt-counterexample.dat --certificate lpt.cert` writes,
for $d = (6, 10)$, $c = (40, 20)$, $t = 5$, $p = 2$:

```text
zeno-certificate 1
instance 2 5 2
d 6 10
dbar 6 10
c 40 20
assume S
front 6
320 48
280 56
260 60
240 64
200 72
160 80
plan 1 2
plane 1 …
…
lower-bounds 5
…
end
```

The points are listed by increasing makespan. `assume S` only: every gap of this front is closed
by the relaxation $L$, so the certificate holds for central flights of any duration. Both checkers
accept it:

```text
$ zeno check lpt.cert
certificate accepted, assuming S
$ lake exe zeno-check lpt.cert
accepted: the 6 points are the Pareto front (all gaps relaxed: for every central flight table; ZenoFront.Cert.check_sound)
```
